kurz: Fat makes baked goods tender because it coats the flour, keeps them moist and carries flavour. Which fat you use decides the texture.
bild_im_kopf: Like a raincoat around the flour: water has a harder time getting in, so the network stays weak.
was_passiert: Solid fat such as cold [[butter|butter]] stays in little pieces and gives layers. Soft butter can be creamed with sugar and holds air. Oil makes cakes especially moist, but cannot hold air.
faustregeln: Cold butter for shortcrust and puff pastry, soft for sponge cakes, oil for moist cakes.
